transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-03 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~47 mins
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Ravi (Redwood SE), Ari (Redwood CSM); Nora (Astral Security), Marcus (Astral Cloud), Priya (Astral Compliance), Jonah (Astral Ops)

Summary:
Quick security/compliance review focused on what admin activity is captured by Redwood, options for exporting evidence to Astral's SIEM/offsite archive, and retention/immutability controls (regulatory context: insurance underwriting and claims). Discussed SOC 2/ISO mapping, RBAC/SSO auditability, KMS/HSM key policies, and export formats. Agreed next steps for schema handoff and a pilot integration with Splunk.

Topics covered:
- What events Redwood captures (api calls, UI admin actions, role changes, policy toggles, key material ops)
- Export methods: on-demand snapshot, continuous stream (kafka), S3 export (ndjson/parquet), secure FTP
- Retention policies + legal hold / e-discovery patterns
- Encryption, key rotation, HSM options, and split-key for enterprise/private deployment
- RBAC/SSO audit trail fidelity (SAML Okta session linkage)
- Evidence packaging for ISO/SOC audits and cross-region residency requirements

00:00:02 Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining. we will do a quick run through of the admin activity capture features then focus on the export + retention questions you shared.
00:00:11 Nora: sounds good, yeah, we want to make sure any admin action that affects policy or data access is captureable and exportable for our regulators.
00:00:18 Liam: perfect. quick intro - i'm liam, i own the infra side for redwood's admin telemetry. we'll walk through what fields are in the events and the export options.
00:00:27 Marcus: quick context — Astral needs 7 years retention for underwriting evidence in our primary region, and 2 years for some operational metadata. also, everything stored in eu must live inside eu, so residency is key.
00:00:41 Ravi: ok that helps. we do region-scoped exports and can replicate to customer-controlled S3 or stream to kafka clusters in-region.
00:00:49 Priya: can you talk about the granularity? like do you log API payloads, or just method names and resource ids? anything with p i i needs to be redacted.
00:00:58 Liam: good question. by default we capture a structured event per action with about 40+ fields: timestamp, actor id, actor email, role at time of action, action type (eg: role.assignment, policy.update, model.deploy), resource id, resource type, request id, status, ip, user_agent, region, causal trace id, and optional request/response blobs for certain ops. blobs are off by default for security conscious customers — we can enable request/response capture for a pilot and apply automatic redaction rules.
00:01:25 Jonah: how deterministic are redaction rules? we need to ensure things like ssn or tax ids are not captured.
00:01:30 Liam: we provide regex-based redaction and PII detectors (token-based). for enterprise, we recommend an allowlist approach: capture meta fields by default and enable blobs only for specific admin flows with manual review. also you can supply custom regex patterns.
00:01:46 Nora: ok. the regulator may ask for a reconstructed timeline for a claim escalation — that means we need full sequences of role changes + session context. does session linkage exist?
00:01:54 Ravi: yes we add session ids and link SAML assertion ids where available, so you can tie an action back to the Okta SSO assertion. note transcription sometimes shows SAML as "Sam-el" in logs, just kidding — but the session field is there.
00:02:10 Marcus: about retention — can we set different retention windows per event type? e.g., admin-role-changes 7 years, debug-level logs 90 days.
00:02:18 Liam: absolutely. retention policies are configurable per-event-class. you can define policy sets per environment and per region. we also support legal hold where retention is extended and exports flagged as evidence.
00:02:29 Priya: evidence packaging — when auditors ask for SOC2 artifacts, do you provide a packaged bundle (digest + manifest) that proves immutability?
00:02:35 Maya: yes, we have an evidence pack option. it creates a time-stamped manifest, cryptographic hashes of exported files, and optional notarization via HSM-backed signing. for customers on private deployments we can integrate with your HSM for signing.
00:02:47 Nora: what's the format of the export? prefer parquet for large volumes but need readable ndjson for quick review.
00:02:52 Liam: exports available as ndjson (newline-delimited json) and parquet. both include the same schema. for streaming we can push avro or ndjson over kafka. S3 export supports server-side encryption with your KMS key.
00:03:06 Marcus: KMS — can you use our key? we use a customer-managed key in cloud hsm.
00:03:11 Ravi: yes. hosted customers can bring-your-own-key (BYOK) via KMS integration. we support CMKs in AWS KMS and external HSMs for dedicated/private. key rotation is supported and we preserve access to older encrypted blobs via key versioning metadata in the manifest.
00:03:25 Priya: are there guidelines around how key rotation affects archived evidence? auditors expect verifiable chain of custody even after rotation.
00:03:31 Liam: that's exactly why the export manifest contains the key id and key version at time of encryption and the HSM signature if enabled. we also keep an immutable audit index for a configurable time that stores event digests — that index is append-only and can be configured to replicate to your region.
00:03:49 Jonah: costs — pushing everything including request/response blobs to S3 at 7 years will be expensive. can we sample or tier?
00:03:56 Maya: yes, common pattern is: full capture for admin/privileged operations, minimal metadata for routine telemetry, and then a tiered cold archive (glacier/cold storage) for long-term retention. Redwood Optimize can also give you cost estimates by event class.
00:04:10 Marcus: residency — if data must stay in eu, and you are hosted in multiple regions, how do we guarantee exports remain in eu?
00:04:16 Ravi: we pin export buckets and streaming endpoints to the region. for example, we can set the S3 export to an eu-only bucket with enforced policy that blocks replication out of eu. for kafka streams we can provision an in-region connector.
00:04:27 Nora: can you talk about immutability? some regulators want write-once storage or WORM.
00:04:33 Liam: we offer options: WORM in S3 (object lock), immutable append-only indices within our platform, and cryptographic signing. on private/dedicated we can also set up hardware-enforced WORM with partner storage.
00:04:45 Priya: do you record admin UI exports? like when someone triggers a manual export from console, is that an event?
00:04:52 Liam: yes, export actions are first-class events with before/after snapshots. we also log the actor, justification, and generated manifest id.
00:04:59 Marcus: SIEM integration — we use Splunk and have an internal ingest pipeline. can Redwood push directly into Splunk or do we have to pull from S3?
00:05:06 Ravi: both. push via HTTP Event Collector (HEC) or a kafka connector into your Splunk deployment. pull via S3 is fine too. we usually recommend an initial pilot with push via HEC to validate schema.
00:05:17 Priya: our legal team also needs chain-of-custody for claims evidence — can the logs be play-backed in order? any order guarantee?
00:05:24 Liam: events include monotonic sequence ids per-region and causal trace ids, so you can reconstruct exact order per-shard. cross-region ordering is best-effort — we include wall-clock timestamps with ns resolution and a causal trace to help stitch.
00:05:36 Nora: about RBAC — we use groups in AD via SAML. are group membership changes audit captured and can they be mapped to old role states?
00:05:43 Maya: yes, role/grp changes are captured. we keep the pre-change and post-change state in the event so you can see the diff.
00:05:50 Jonah: is there a retention policy override for security investigations? sometimes we need to bump retention quickly.
00:05:55 Liam: you can raise a legal hold via API or console; that flags events and prevents GC. holds can be scoped to resource types or entire accounts.
00:06:03 Marcus: do you have examples of exported manifests?
00:06:06 Maya: we have a short sample in the repo, i'll send a link — https://redwood.ai/security/audit-playbook.pdf (note: sample manifest on page 12).
00:06:14 Priya: great. for SOC2 evidence, do you map events to Trust Services Criteria?
00:06:19 Liam: yes we have a mapping matrix for SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 controls. we'll include that with the schema handoff.
00:06:26 Nora: what about tamper detection? if someone with elevated access tries to delete events, how is that visible?
00:06:31 Ravi: deletions are themselves logged as admin events and the immutable index records hashes — any mismatch triggers an alert. on hosted we also offer external webhook notifications for deletion events so you can ingest into your monitoring.
00:06:43 Marcus: can you explain the difference between inference logs and admin logs? our data team keeps mixing these up.
00:06:48 Liam: inference logs are request/response pairs for model inference (user inputs, outputs) — generally higher-volume and more sensitive. admin logs are operations against the control plane (role changes, model rollout, billing config). we keep them separate and have separate retention/PII defaults.
00:07:02 Priya: on masking - if we need to retain an event but redact sensitive fields, do you store redacted pre-images?
00:07:08 Liam: we store redacted blobs; for provenance we can keep deterministic hashes of the original content in the manifest so you can validate integrity but not expose the PII.
00:07:17 Maya: ok, quick recap before we move to next steps. we will: share the full export schema + sample files, include mapping to SOC2/ISO controls, provide KMS/HSM runbook options, and propose a short pilot to stream admin events into Astral's Splunk.
00:07:31 Priya: that sounds right. one more thing — do you support cross-account encryption where the manifest is signed by our key and redwood's key?
00:07:38 Ravi: yes hybrid signing is supported — dual-signature in manifest, and we can include both key IDs.
00:07:44 Jonah: any gotchas for on-prem/private deployments?
00:07:47 Liam: network egress — for air-gapped installs we produce local evidence packs and can hand off physical media. also, some integrators require a connector to the internal Kafka cluster — we have that pattern.
00:07:59 Nora: perfect. let's talk timeline: we need the schema this week, internal review next week, then pilot.
00:08:05 Maya: noted. action items will reflect that.

Questions (raised live):
- Will exports include full request/response blobs by default? (no, off by default)
- Can we use our CMK/HSM? (yes)
- Is there WORM/immutable option? (yes — S3 object lock / append-only index / HSM signing)
- Can admin exports be pushed to Splunk? (yes — HEC or kafka connector)

Closing (approx 15:08 UTC):
00:08:15 Maya: thanks everyone, we'll send the schema and SOC2 mapping after the call. expect me to follow up with meeting notes and pilot options.
00:08:23 Nora: thanks — appreciate it.
00:08:25 Marcus: thanks all.
